the molting process of the domestic goose, as well as the postnuptial, prenuptial and postmolting periods of the sexual repose, are under the control of the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis.
the molting process is controlled by the gonadal steroids, the adrenal steroids and the thyroid hormones.
the molting process in domestic goose is controlled by the interaction of gonadal and adrenocortical steroids and thyroid hormones, and the role of these hormones in molting is sex-dependent.

the role of gonadal, adrenal and thyroid hormones in molting of domestic goose.
the regulation of molt by the gonadal and adrenal steroid hormones and thyroid hormones in domestic geese.
the changes of plasma steroid and thyroid hormone concentrations during molting and sexual repose in geese.

the molting is regulated by the gonadal and adrenal steroid hormones and thyroid hormones in both sexes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) in the postnuptial mol, the molt is induced by the elevated plasma B concentration, (2) in the prenuptail molt, the molt is controlled by the high T3 concentration, (3) in the postmolting stage, the molt is terminated by the elevated T, T4 and P4 levels, (4) in the preparatory stage the molt is terminated and/or inhibited by the increased B concentration.
the molting process is controlled by a number of factors, but the main one is the thyroid hormone, which is responsible for the outgrowth of feathers.

the molt is controlled by the interaction of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (HPA) and gonadal axis (GA) in both sexes, and thyroid hormones (TH) play a role in the regulation of molt in ganders, but in geese, the role of TH is limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gonadal and adrenal hormones are not the primary factors controlling the molt in the goose.
in the domestic goose, as in other bird species, the molting is regulated by gonadal, adrenal and thyroid hormones.
the gonadal and adrenal steroid and thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of molt in geese.
